definition: A strong love of the work itself, which he ranks above connections or wealth.
example: You may not have connections, or an education, or wealth, but with enough passion and sweat, you can make anything happen.

definition: Hard effort spent in place of money, the cost he says a personal brand actually requires.
example: With enough passion and sweat, you can make anything happen.

definition: The platform and moment in which a message is seen, which he ranks above the message itself.
example: Content is king, but context is God.

definition: The stories, jokes, and useful pieces you give an audience before you ask for anything.
example: Content is king, but context is God.

definition: The setup that makes a later ask feel earned rather than sudden.
example: There is no sale without the story; no knockout without the setup.

definition: The finishing ask or sale, which has no power without the jabs that came first.
example: There is no sale without the story; no knockout without the setup.

definition: Real back-and-forth with an audience, as distinct from talking at them.
example: There's a lot of talking and selling on Twitter, but not enough engagement.

definition: A distorted, almost absurd misuse of something — here, using a listening medium only to sell.
example: Not enough engagement, and that's a travesty, because Twitter is the cocktail party of the Internet.

definition: In a way that is genuinely meant, not performed for the feed.
example: Only the companies that mind their manners in an old-fashioned way — and do it authentically — are going to have a prayer of competing.

definition: The old habits of courtesy that he says decide who can compete once every customer has a voice.
example: Only the companies that can figure out how to mind their manners in a very old-fashioned way are going to compete.

definition: What a community treats as valuable. Here, caring is the coin of a small town.
example: Vibrant towns were dominated by the strength of relationships, the currency of caring, and the power of word of mouth.

definition: Taking each customer's stake personally, which he treats as a business advantage.
example: The currency of caring, and the power of word of mouth, still run a small town.

definition: An ongoing tie with a person, stronger in his account than a one-time pitch.
example: Social media made one great big small town, dominated by the strength of relationships.

definition: The piece a structure rests on. He wants caring installed there, not added later.
example: Install caring as your business's cornerstone, or be willing to embark on a cultural overhaul.

definition: A thorough rebuilding, here of a culture that does not yet know how to care in public.
example: If caring is not the cornerstone, you have to be willing to embark on a cultural overhaul.

definition: To pass from person to person, as talk about a company does.
example: Companies have to shape the word of mouth that circulates about them.

definition: Full of life and exchange, the kind of town where word of mouth decided reputations.
example: Social media turned the world into one great big small town, dominated as all vibrant towns used to be.

definition: The person who might buy, and whom he says must be treated as the most important one.
example: Treat each customer as though he or she were the most important customer in the world.

definition: A light piece of content that gives the audience something before any sales punch.
example: Jabs are the lightweight pieces of content that benefit your customers by making them laugh or feel appreciated.

definition: To feel that one's attention was valued, which a jab is meant to produce.
example: Jabs benefit your customers by making them laugh, snicker, feel appreciated, or escape.

definition: Very great in effect. He uses it for the payoff of listening before you sell.
example: Twitter is a place where listening well has tremendous benefits.

definition: To move someone to act, not merely to notice.
example: Your story isn't powerful enough if it only leads the horse to water; it has to inspire the horse to drink, too.
